bug_semantics: An authenticated backend user could submit the self-service account save handler with an attacker-chosen form_context such as update. FormController trusted that POST value over the server-selected myaccount context, so Users::formExtendFields treated the request as an administrative user form and admitted role, individual-permission, and superuser-related fields into the form widget's save data. The handler still selected the attacker's own User model, allowing protected authorization attributes to be mass-updated and the account to gain higher backend privileges.
flaw_origin: Commit 94a4ccb6abccd025e7e201590999061574ffdeb9 made the Users controller's self-service mysettings action unrestricted by setting requiredPermissions to null. That small authorization change was the first point at which ordinary authenticated backend users could reach the already-existing unsafe composition of mysettings_onSave and POST-controlled FormController context selection; its parent still required backend.manage_users for the controller, so the low-privilege attack path was absent there.
ai_marker: absent: the BIC commit object names human author Sam Georges <sam@daftspunk.com> and human committer Sam Georges <sam@daftspunk.com>, and its message contains only 'Ref #306 - mysettings should be unrestricted by permissions' with no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other AI trailer/marker.
evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/wintercms/winter/security/advisories/GHSA-pgpf-m8m4-6cg6 states that any authenticated backend user could escalate by modifying roles/permissions through crafted backend requests and identifies patched versions 1.0.477, 1.1.12, and 1.2.12.

git show 94a4ccb6abccd025e7e201590999061574ffdeb9 shows a one-file, three-line semantic change in modules/backend/controllers/Users.php: for action mysettings it assigns $this->requiredPermissions = null; the subject explicitly says 'mysettings should be unrestricted by permissions'. This is smaller and causally later than the latent form-context/save machinery introduced in 71a5dd67ab9e0d0da7caabd3fb5aaa3d86bb45e5.

Direct parent-tree verification with git blame/show at 0b8c8a0c0f616084c64747a31908efd1a470000b shows modules/backend/controllers/Users.php still has public $requiredPermissions = ['backend.manage_users'] and its constructor contains no action-specific nulling of that requirement. The 94a4ccb6 parent diff therefore proves the low-privilege reachability change is absent at the immediate parent.

History inspection of the vulnerable pre-fix tree (v1.2.11) shows modules/backend/controllers/Users.php::myaccount_onSave calling FormController::update_onSave for the current user's ID and formExtendFields returning early only for context myaccount. modules/backend/behaviors/FormController.php::initForm then calls formGetContext(), whose vulnerable implementation returns post('form_context', $this->context). A crafted non-myaccount context consequently exposes protected user fields to getSaveData while retaining the self-account target.

git show d69e8415faafae409aaa046e1179b65364aad226 directly fixes both layers: FormController::formGetContext no longer reads POST and initForm preserves the server-selected context, while modules/backend/models/User.php::beforeSave rejects self changes to role_id, is_superuser, or permissions and enforces manage-users/superuser authorization. The same fix was backported as 7d6258703f1da2fdadb10e3a2d0c7d09ac2ae782 (tag v1.0.477) and 76b57bccbb14b957b7981e43e0a5a969db220607 (tag v1.1.12).

Tag membership checks show the BIC in vulnerable boundary tags v1.0.476, v1.1.11, and v1.2.11 as well as their patched successors. The 1.0 backport is contained in v1.0.477 but not v1.0.476; the 1.1 backport is contained in v1.1.12 but not v1.1.11; and d69e8415faafae409aaa046e1179b65364aad226 is contained in v1.2.12 but not v1.2.11. The v1.2.12 tag resolves to b6ac66c5e80ddc9ecd9211c10204cdcee6e14313, which contains the direct fix.

git cat-file -p 94a4ccb6abccd025e7e201590999061574ffdeb9 gives parent 0b8c8a0c0f616084c64747a31908efd1a470000b, author and committer Sam Georges, and a message with no trailers. Only this BIC commit object was used for AI attribution.
reasoning: The advisory's attack requires both a self-service save path reachable by a user without backend.manage_users and a way for that path to accept fields reserved for an administrative user form. The latter pieces existed in the initial public code: the self-save handler targeted the current user, FormController let POST form_context override the trusted context, and Users conditionally added permission fields based on that context. They were latent for the stated low-privilege attacker while the Users controller required backend.manage_users. Commit 94a4ccb6abccd025e7e201590999061574ffdeb9 is therefore the smallest real BIC: it changes only the reachability guard and first makes mysettings available without permissions, completing the exploit path. Its direct parent retains the controller-wide backend.manage_users requirement and lacks the override, establishing parent absence. The BIC predates all affected 1.0/1.1/1.2 ranges, and the three branch-specific fix commits land exactly in the advisory's first patched tags. The fix removes client control of context and adds model-level authorization defense in depth. Because the BIC commit object is a 2014 human-authored/committed change with no AI or bot marker or trailer, the BIC-only attribution verdict is NOT_AI.
